description: Heat Stress Metrics for US Census Tracts 1998–2020 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Rouzbeh Rahai et al. Extreme heat exposure is a growing public health threat. Heat-health research has commonly used dry-bulb temperature to characterize heat exposure, partly due to limited availability of spatially explicit, public-health-aligned datasets that integrate multiple meteorological factors to quantify heat stress. Coverage: not stated; published in 2026. Formats: Parquet, Image. The data are held in Figshare+ and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 554531072596 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
